workflow: A container operation scans entries while retaining pointers and a count for its backing storage, then invokes user-defined comparison behavior.
The callback re-enters and mutates the same container, clearing or resizing its storage and changing the recorded count.
The original operation resumes with stale pointer and count assumptions and continues scanning beyond the valid allocation.
An out-of-bounds read causes a heap-buffer-overflow and process termination instead of safe reentrant handling.
summary: Reentrant container mutation invalidates active storage traversal
decision_reason: The failure workflow is materially the same as re-entrant cleanup invalidating container storage during an active clearing operation: user-controlled re-entry mutates the container while the original traversal retains stale storage and accounting state, leading to an out-of-bounds access.
